display.purpose: The ASCII banner on the start screen only, filled with the spectrum gradient.

headline.purpose: The lead sentence on the start screen (--t-xl).

body.purpose: Default interface text: buttons, fields, rows, menus (--t).

prose.purpose: Paragraphs and text areas; a line is as tall as a list row (line-height φ).

label.purpose: Status bar, counts, tags, kbd, hints (--t-s).

mono.purpose: code, kbd, pre in Recursive's strict monospace; always left to right.

shadows.name: --shadow-float
shadows.purpose: Bars floating over a view (find, reconnect) and the hint over a detached window.

shadows.name: --shadow-menu
shadows.purpose: Context menus, dropdown lists and toasts.

shadows.name: --shadow-dialog
shadows.purpose: Modal dialogs and the command palette.

motion.name: --ease-out
motion.purpose: Arrivals: fast to where they land, then settle.

motion.name: float-in
motion.purpose: Dialogs, the palette, find and reconnect bars, toasts: a fade from 5px short of where they hang (--from, -5px for top-hung).

motion.name: fade-in
motion.purpose: The scrim behind a dialog or the palette, and the lock screen.

motion.name: focus-ring
motion.purpose: The focused pane's ring glides to the next pane; no transition while an edge is dragged.

motion.name: toast-out
motion.purpose: A toast leaves faster than it came (Svelte out:fade, 0 under reduced motion).

motion.name: search-open
motion.purpose: The sidebar search field opens out from its button.

motion.name: caret
motion.purpose: A folder's caret turning open or closed.

motion.name: step-back
motion.purpose: Chrome dims to 45% while the sidebar search is open.

motion.name: drop-zone
motion.purpose: Pane drop zones lighting up under a dragged tab.

motion.name: anodize
motion.purpose: The banner's spectrum runs across it once on arrival.

motion.name: found
motion.purpose: A gold wash held, then fading off the setting a search went to (Settings.svelte).

motion.name: outline-breathe
motion.purpose: Broadcast outline style: a 16px inner glow swells and settles.

motion.name: outline-ring
motion.purpose: Broadcast outline style (also rainbow): a conic sweep around the pane.

motion.name: outline-march
motion.purpose: Broadcast outline style: 45° stripes walking along the edge.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Every animation and transition collapses under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: outline-fade
motion.purpose: Broadcast outline style: the colour dims to 25% and back.

narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Anodized Rack"**

xtermium is a rack of live connections. The chrome is cool titanium, a stack of blue-grey metals that get lighter the nearer they sit to the hand. Each kind of connection gets the colour titanium turns when anodized, the way cables on a patch panel are colour-coded: SSH is cobalt, RDP violet, serial chartreuse. One brushed-gold accent marks where you are and what you picked. Nothing else is coloured, so a glance at the rack tells you which kind of session each row and tab is, and a glance at the gold tells you where the keyboard is.

The feel is machined and quiet, as dense as a modern code editor: 13px system text, 26px controls, 21px rows, small precise corners. The sidebar (the session rack), the tab area with its panes, and the file panel are rounded panels floating a few pixels apart on a darker window. They are flat at rest and are told apart by tone, not by shadow. Only things that float above the work cast a shadow: menus, dialogs, the command palette, toasts.

Every proportion comes from the golden ratio (φ ≈ 1.618). Spacing steps along the Fibonacci scale, padding pairs go 1 : φ from vertical to horizontal, type steps by a quarter of φ, and dialogs are 377, 610 or 987px wide. Settings is a golden rectangle, 987 × 610. `ui/lib/scale.test.ts` enforces the spacing and type scales in `npm test`, so they are rules, not guidelines.
keyCharacteristics: Titanium neutrals in six tonal steps, a dark theme by default and a full light theme.
One accent, Brushed Gold, which the user can change. It is never decoration.
Ten anodized hues, one per kind of connection, used only to say "this is an SSH/RDP/… thing".
Fibonacci spacing (1 2 3 5 8 13 21 34px) and five type sizes, both enforced by a test.
Rounded panels on a darker window. Flat at rest; shadows only on floating layers.
Icon-only tool buttons with tooltips. Boxicons SVGs, animated only on session rows and tabs.
Right-to-left ready: logical properties throughout, with flips for chevrons, menus and carets.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Gold says "you are here" or "you picked this", and nothing else. Two exceptions: the fill of a dialog's single primary button, and a folder's tag (`.tag`, `prod`, `lab`…), which is a fact about where you are and shows on the folder's row and under a pane. No gold headings, icons or decorative strokes.

rules.name: The Cable Colour Rule
rules.body: A kind hue identifies a kind of connection and nothing else, and nothing else takes its place: a session's icon is always in its kind's hue, whatever it is marked with. State (connected, waiting, failed) is always `ok` / `warn` / `error`, never a kind hue.

rules.name: The See-Through Chrome Rule
rules.body: Chrome backgrounds are written `rgba(var(--panel-rgb), var(--chrome-alpha))` (or the `window`/`bg`/`deep` triplet), never as a hex. `--chrome-alpha` drops below 1 while a window effect is on, and the desktop shows through.

rules.name: The Five Sizes Rule
rules.body: Every `font-size` is a type token (`var(--t-s)` … `var(--t-xxl)`), `inherit`, an `em`, or a `clamp()`. A raw `px` size fails `npm test`.

rules.name: The Golden Line Rule
rules.body: Prose and text areas set `line-height: var(--phi)`. Dense UI text stays at 1.4.

rules.name: The Fibonacci Rule
rules.body: Padding, margin, gap, inset and border-radius values are Fibonacci pixels. A stray 4px or 12px fails `npm test`.

rules.name: The Derived Value Rule
rules.body: A value worked out from others is written as `calc(…)` so it reads as derived: `calc(8px + 16px + 5px)` is a field's text start past its icon, and `calc(var(--r-menu) - 3px)` is a menu item's corner.

rules.name: The Float-Only Shadow Rule
rules.body: A surface casts a shadow only if it floats over the work and goes away again, and takes it from one of the three tokens. Panels, tabs, rows and buttons never do.

rules.name: The Nested Curve Rule
rules.body: A rounded thing inside another keeps the same curve: its radius is the outer one less the room between them, written as `calc()` (a menu item is `calc(var(--r-menu) - 3px)`, a segmented button `calc(var(--r-control) - 1px)`).

dos: Do use only Fibonacci pixels for spacing and radii (1 2 3 5 8 13 21 34), with padding in 1 : φ pairs (`3px 8px`, `5px 8px`, `8px 13px`).
Do set every text size from the type tokens (`--t-s --t --t-l --t-xl --t-xxl`).
Do size things with `--row` (21px), `--control` (26px) and `--bar` (34px), and write any derived value as `calc(…)`.
Do keep gold for focus, selection, toggles that are on, links, drop targets and the one primary action. Read it as `var(--gold)`, since the user can change it.
Do colour a session by its kind hue (icon, tab connector, glyph tile) through `--kind`.
Do paint chrome as `rgba(var(--…-rgb), var(--chrome-alpha))` so window effects show through.
Do end a menu with its destructive item (`.danger`) and start groups with `.sep`.
Do offer Undo instead of a question when the thing can be put back, and ask (with a danger button) only when it can't: a running connection, a folder of sessions, a restore.

Do focus the safe answer when yes can't be undone or is a security call (Reject on a new host key, Cancel on a delete or restore, Keep editing on discard), so Enter never does the irreversible thing; an ordinary yes (Close tab, which Reopen can undo) keeps the focus.
Do make tool buttons icon-only with a tooltip.

Do keep motion to state and continuity: 0.1–0.2s, arrivals on `--ease-out`, a new floating layer through `float-in`, exits faster than entrances. CSS motion stops under `prefers-reduced-motion` through `ui/app.css`; a Svelte transition must check it itself.
Do use logical properties (`inset-inline-*`, `margin-inline-*`) so right-to-left mirrors.
donts: Don't use off-scale spacing (4px, 6px, 10px, 12px, 16px) or a raw `font-size` in px; the scale test fails on them.
Don't put a shadow on a resting panel, tab, row or button, or write a new shadow value for a floating layer: use `--shadow-float`, `--shadow-menu` or `--shadow-dialog`.
Don't use gold for headings, icons, illustration or large fills other than the primary button.
Don't use a kind hue to show state, or a status colour to mean a kind of connection.
Don't let a user's colour recolour a session's icon: marks go on names (`.tinted`) and tab lines, and accent presets stay off the kind hues and the error red.
Don't hard-code the accent's hex, or the chrome as an opaque hex.
Don't animate the interface's own icons. Only session and folder icons move, and only on hover.
Don't add big padding or wide gaps. The densest comfortable layout is the house style.
Don't use the spectrum gradient anywhere but the start screen's banner, where it plays once.
